SYNTHESIS FOR THE TWO DELIVERABLES:
(1) China has a funded memory-native champion: MemTensor/MemOS — ~RMB 100M Pre-A (Jul 20 2026) from Huawei/Honor/SenseTime, SJTU-linked research (arXiv 2507.03724), 11k-star Apache-2.0 OSS, cloud tiers, enterprise logos (Trip.com, Haier, China Telecom, Alibaba Cloud). Funding pattern is strategic-CVC/state-adjacent, vs US memory startups' VC pattern (Mem0: $24M from YC/Peak XV, Nov 4 2025 per QQ headline, gnews id CBMiVkFVX3lxTE1rVnhIZWFTQ1BBX3plRE9fa3FUWllzZjNaZDhkRlloMkIxc2FidEt6T0g1NDZvMVJMYk5vV0gySjhYX3ZsQ0JlbVZRdXNnSmhjanZ0MXNB). State capital dominates at the top: DeepSeek's first round reportedly Big-Fund-led ($45B pre-money May 2026, ~$7B at ~$59B by June per headlines); Big Fund's first embodied-AI bet was 银河通用 RMB 2.5B (Mar 2 2026, per 财联社 headline).
(2) Platform giveaway + open weights = commoditization: Bailian long-term memory is free (storage AND memory tokens uncharged per docs); ByteDance open-sourced Coze Studio (Apache 2.0, 21.5k stars); Dify at 153.4k stars is self-hostable; DeepSeek V4 (MIT, 1M context, Jul-Aug 2026) lets anyone self-host long context. Severe pricing pressure on any paid US context product's China-comparable feature set.
(3) Market access closing both ways: NDRC blocked Meta's ~$2B Manus buy (Apr 27 2026; unwound Jun 15 2026; Manus independent Aug 11 2026); 'Singapore washing' red lines (Asia Times May 1 2026); Beijing urging startups to refuse US money (per headlines). Meanwhile Chinese-founded Genspark ($2.6B, Jun 2026) competes freely in the US and markets 'context, not models' (Jul 21 2026). US context startups face a closed China market (xinchuang on-prem procurement, 双备案 dual filing, PIPL, new 《智能体新规》 agent rules) AND China-diaspora competition at home.
(4) Context economics whiplash: permanent price cuts H1 2026 (DeepSeek V4-Pro to 1/4 price May 25 2026; Xiaomi followed May 27) then Aug 2026 inversion — DeepSeek raising/off-peak-discounting while OpenAI cuts, driven by agent token-volume explosion (QQ Aug 18 2026); Doubao ended the subsidy era (May 12 2026). Cheap tokens weaken 'save tokens' pitches, but agent volume makes context management a cost-control necessity — supports the US context-startup thesis on economics even as it undercuts it on moat.

private.title: Private markets: funding trends and what investors expect
private.takeaway: AI took 80% of a record $510B H1 2026 venture market, with OpenAI and Anthropic alone absorbing 43% of all startup funding; entry prices carry an 84% Series A premium while exits only selectively reopened (15 VC-backed IPOs in Q1, then SpaceX's $1.77T debut and Anysphere's $60B acquisition in Q2). Named investor theses (Sequoia, Bessemer, YC) converge on agent memory/context/harness infrastructure — the exact layer MIT's 95%-pilot-failure finding diagnoses as the gap — but actual context-infra rounds (Mem0 $24M, Cognee €7.5M) remain orders of magnitude smaller than lab mega-rounds, and Anthropic's ~$2T IPO is the repricing event everything now waits on.
private.notes: Verified on primary pages: Crunchbase H1 2026 ($510B, $217B/43%, Q1 $305B, Q2 exits incl. SpaceX $1.77T IPO and Anysphere $60B M&A), Crunchbase Q1 concentration (80% AI share, top-4 $188B = ~65%, NA dollars +190% vs deals -26%), Anthropic Series H ($65B at $965B, $47B run-rate), xAI Series E ($20B, above $15B target), Institutional Investor/PitchBook (15 IPOs Q1 2026, 84%/55% premiums, $278.5B dry powder, 14.6% IRR, recovery-to-2027 warning), Fortune/MIT NANDA (95% pilots, 150 interviews/350 surveys/300 deployments, cause = tools that don't learn/adapt), Sequoia services thesis, Bessemer five frontiers (organizational amnesia, 78% invisible failures), YC Fall 2026 RFS (Multiplayer AI, Self-Maintaining APIs, Cloud for Small Software), TechCrunch Mem0 ($24M = $3.9M seed + $20M A; 35M→186M API calls; exclusive AWS Agent SDK memory provider). Blocked fetches marked per-headline in fragment: CNBC OpenAI $122B page (403; round size independently confirmed by fetched Crunchbase page; $852B valuation per SiliconANGLE/tech-insider headlines), Business Insider Anthropic $1.5T secondary (blocked host). xAI valuation (~$235B) is per NextBigFuture headline only; SSI, Moonshot, Zhipu, MiniMax, Mistral, Menlo $37B, Tangen, Dudley, JPMorgan items carried per sweep headlines with outlet+date labels. Caps used: 12/12 WebFetch, 3/8 search calls.

usvschina.title: US vs China: the competitive investment picture
usvschina.takeaway: One AI boom, two capital systems: the US concentrates record private mega-rounds (OpenAI+Anthropic = $217B, 43% of H1 2026 global VC; Anthropic at $965B) into a handful of closed-weight labs still waiting on IPOs, while China runs a state-anchored, public-market-first system — Zhipu and MiniMax already listed in HK, Moonshot at $35B heading to IPO, DeepSeek's $7.4B round giving voting rights only to the state, and a $295B national buildout plan — with flagship valuations roughly 25x apart but public multiples inverted.
usvschina.notes: Verified on primary pages: Anthropic Series H ($65B at $965B, May 28 2026, $47B run-rate, $15B hyperscalers incl $5B Amazon); xAI Series E ($20B, Jan 6 2026, Nvidia/Cisco/QIA/MGX, 1M+ H100-equivalents); Crunchbase H1 2026 ($510B global, OpenAI+Anthropic $217B=43%) and Q1 2026 (AI=80% of global VC; top-4 US rounds $188B~65%); Institutional Investor/PitchBook (15 VC-backed IPOs Q1 2026, 84% Series A AI premium, $278.5B dry powder, ~$3T OpenAI/Anthropic/SpaceX liquidity-absorption warning); 21jingji (Moonshot $2B at >$20B May 7 2026, valuation path, DeepSeek Big Fund talks at ~$45B under negotiation); cls.cn (Zhipu IPO tutoring Apr 2025 w/CICC, ¥40B pre-IPO valuation, MiniMax Shanghai-state C round); wallstreetcn (Zhipu ~¥1T cap end-Jun 2026, ~20x since listing, ¥724M 2025 revenue, MiniMax −60% from >HK$400B peak, OpenAI ~35x forward multiple quote). Fetch failures: CNBC OpenAI $122B (403 — figure confirmed via Crunchbase instead), Business Insider $1.5T secondary (blocked — cited per headline), Google News redirector did not reveal The Decoder target. Headline-level (multi-outlet) items marked "per headline" throughout: Moonshot $3.5B at $35B (Bloomberg + Silicon Republic + Unite.AI + The Standard, Jul 29), $50B pre-IPO round (财联社 Aug 5), 股改/HK IPO (Sina Aug 21), $295B plan (Bloomberg/Reuters Jun 9; 80% domestic-chip requirement per The Decoder headline), DeepSeek $7.4B at $50B ($59B some reports) with sole-state voting rights (Forbes/Tech Times/Tech Funding News Jun 16-17), USD funds −84% (Sina Jan 8), H200 China sales zero (EE Times China Feb 25), Cambricon ~$143B (Jun 18). Caveat: the small-model summaries of the two Chinese pages misread scale on two figures (Zhipu HK cap, MiniMax C-round valuation); I used the sweep's originals (¥362.7B on May 7; MiniMax C round >$4B/~¥30B) which are consistent with the verified 20x-to-¥1T and −60%-from-HK$400B trajectories. gapSections.title: 2026-dated rounds for US context/memory/RAG startups beyond Mem0 and Cognee
gapSections.takeaway: The "orders of magnitude smaller" claim now rests on eight 2026-dated context/memory/RAG rounds instead of two 2025 datapoints: Feb-Jun 2026 rounds range $2.3M-$250M (sum ~$461M, under 0.4% of OpenAI's single $122B March close). Largest is Exa's $250M Series C at $2.2B (May 20, 2026, a16z-led), ~490x below OpenAI's round. The 2023-cohort flagships (LangChain, Pinecone, Letta, LlamaIndex) show no 2026 primary rounds — Qdrant's $50M Series B (Mar 12) is the lone exception — while corporate strategics (Nvidia, Bosch, Ricoh) are the distinctive buyers at this layer.
gapSections.notes: Verified against publisher pages: Exa $250M Series C @ $2.2B led by Andreessen Horowitz, May 20 2026 (SiliconANGLE); Qdrant $50M Series B led by AVP with Bosch Ventures, $87.8M total, Mar 12 2026 (SiliconANGLE); CopilotKit $27M Series A (Glilot/NFX/SignalFire), Seattle, May 5 2026 (TechCrunch); Reload $2.275M led by Anthemis, shared structured memory for agent workforces, Feb 19 2026 (TechCrunch); Ricoh->Weaviate undisclosed strategic investment, invested Mar 13 2026, announced Jun 16 2026 (ricoh.com release). Per-headline only: Engram $98M @ $600M with 13 employees (Calcalist, Jun 23 2026 — sector and HQ UNVERIFIED, do not use as load-bearing); SageOx $15M Seattle (GeekWire URL real but 403); Seltz $12.5M seed (Fortune); Manufact $6.3M MCP (VentureBeat); Interloom EUR 14.2M seed (EU-Startups, German). Caveats: Qdrant is Berlin-founded and Weaviate Amsterdam-based, so the strict "US" framing needs those flags; GetLatka valuation/ARR figures (Pinecone $750M valuation Jul 3 2026; Letta $1.4M est ARR; LlamaIndex $10.9M ARR, both Aug 10 2026) are low-reliability third-party estimates cited per headline. The absence of 2026 primary rounds for LangChain/Letta/Pinecone-class names is a verified-negative from targeted gnews queries, not a coverage gap. Ratio math in fragment: median round ~$21M = ~5,800x below OpenAI's $122B; eight-round sum $461M = 0.38% of OpenAI's round and ~0.09% of H1 2026's $510B global venture total. Caps usage: 8/8 search-helper calls, 10 WebFetch (2 wasted on unresolvable Google News redirectors, 1 SageOx 403, 1 navigational), well under time cap.
